reading.body:
Meta has invested $2.5 billion in this Sarpy County campus since groundbreaking in 2017 and employs over 300 people in operations. The campus does not publish its power capacity, so its scale relative to other AI infrastructure cannot be read from operator specifications. No data center in Nebraska has published power figures to this research site, placing this facility's actual megawattage outside the mapped landscape of disclosed U.S. AI compute footprint.

Meta reports that campus electricity is matched with 100 percent renewable energy, with a separate Meta-supported project adding 320 megawatts of renewable capacity to the state. Operations buildings hold LEED Gold certification. The campus is not quantified in terms of racks, accelerators, or AI training density because the operator does not publish megawatt figures, making it impossible to estimate how many training clusters or inference instances it can host.

This campus matters to understanding Meta's infrastructure footprint and Nebraska's role in hyperscale deployment. It does not yet matter to tracking the grid constraint on AI scaling, because Meta has chosen not to publish the power draw that would place it in the constraint analysis. The existence of 320 new megawatts of renewable energy tied to this site signals a material commitment to power availability in the region, but the binding effect on AI scaling cannot be assessed without disclosure of actual IT load.
